questions.text: The book form posts to /books, and BookController's store method handles it. Fill in routes/web.php.
questions.code:
<?php

use App\Http\Controllers\___;
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Route;

Route::get('/', function () {
    return view('books.create');
});

Route::___('/books', [BookController::class, '___']);
questions.explanation: The controller is imported with use App\Http\Controllers\BookController;, the form submits with POST so the route is Route::post(), and the array's second item is the method name, 'store'.

questions.text: Going straight to /books in the browser gives 405 Method Not Allowed, because only a POST route exists for that URL. Add the route that shows the form there too.
questions.explanation: Typing a URL into the address bar sends a GET request. With only Route::post on /books, Laravel finds the URL but not the method, so it answers 405. A Route::get returning view('books.create') fixes it.

questions.text: Capture the book's id from the URL and give the route the name books.show.
questions.explanation: Route parameters go in curly braces, {id}, and are passed to the method's $id argument. ->name('books.show') names the route so you can link to it with route('books.show', $book).

questions.text: Complete the Artisan command that generates app/Http/Controllers/BookController.php.
questions.explanation: php artisan make:controller BookController creates the controller class in app/Http/Controllers.

questions.text: Fill in the controller's namespace, the Request import and the class declaration.
questions.code:
<?php

namespace App\Http\___;

use App\Models\Book;
use Illuminate\Http\___;

class BookController ___ Controller
{
    public function store(Request $request)
    {
        //
    }
}
questions.explanation: Controllers live in the App\Http\Controllers namespace, the request class is Illuminate\Http\Request, and every controller extends Controller (the base class in the same folder).

questions.text: Read the submitted title field from the request.
questions.explanation: $request->input('title') returns that form field's value. $request->title works too, but this blank is a method call.

questions.text: Run the request through validation. If it fails, Laravel sends the user back to the form with the errors.
questions.explanation: $request->validate([...]) checks the rules. On failure it redirects back with $errors and the old input. On success it returns only the validated fields.

questions.text: The title must be filled in and be 3 to 120 characters long.
questions.explanation: required rejects an empty field, and for a string min:3 and max:120 count characters.

questions.text: The subtitle can be left blank. If it is filled in, it must be a string of at most 100 characters.
questions.explanation: nullable allows an empty field, which arrives as null, so string and max only apply when there is a value. Without it, an empty subtitle fails the string rule.

questions.text: The author's name may only contain letters and spaces. Fill in the characters that the regex needs around the pattern so PHP's preg_match accepts it.
questions.explanation: PHP regexes need delimiters: the first character opens the pattern and a matching one has to close it. 'regex:^[a-zA-Z ]+$' fails with "No ending delimiter '^' found". It must be 'regex:/^[a-zA-Z ]+$/'.

questions.text: An ISBN starts with 978 or 979, followed by 10 more digits. The regex contains |, so the rules can't be one pipe-separated string. Fill in what wraps the rules instead.
questions.explanation: Laravel splits a rule string on |, which would cut (978|979) in half. In array syntax, ['required', 'regex:/^(978|979)\d{10}$/'], each rule is its own item, so the pipe in the pattern is left alone.

questions.text: No two books may share an ISBN. Check the isbn column of the books table.
questions.explanation: unique:table,column fails if the value already exists in that column. The column is named because the form field (isbn_code) has a different name.

questions.text: A member's email must have valid RFC syntax and a domain with real DNS records. Name the RFC check first, then the DNS check.
questions.explanation: email:rfc,dns checks the address against RFC syntax and looks up the domain's DNS/MX records. (spoof needs PHP's intl extension, so leave it out unless intl is enabled.)

questions.text: The published date must be a valid date earlier than today.
questions.explanation: date makes sure the value parses as a date, and before:today rejects today and any later date.

questions.text: The number of copies must be a whole number from 1 to 20.
questions.explanation: integer makes between:1,20 compare the number itself. Without a numeric rule, between would count the characters of the string.

questions.text: The genre comes from a dropdown. Accept only the three listed values.
questions.explanation: in:a,b,c only passes if the value is one of the listed items, which stops someone sending a value that isn't in the dropdown.

questions.text: Replace the default message shown when the ISBN fails its regex rule.
questions.explanation: The second argument to validate() holds custom messages, keyed field.rule, so 'isbn.regex' only replaces the regex failure message.

questions.text: Complete the form tag and add the token Laravel requires on every POST form.
questions.explanation: The form method must match Route::post, and @csrf outputs a hidden _token field. Without it, the submission fails with 419 Page Expired.

questions.text: After a failed validation, put the title the user typed back into the input.
questions.explanation: old('title') reads the input flashed to the session by the failed validation, so the user doesn't have to retype it.

questions.text: Mark the input red and show its error message under it when title fails validation.
questions.explanation: @error('title') ... @enderror only renders its contents when that field has an error, which adds Bootstrap's is-invalid class. Inside the block, $message is the first error message for that field.

questions.text: Show every validation error in a list at the top of the form.
questions.explanation: $errors->any() is true when there's at least one error, $errors->all() returns every message as an array, and @foreach is closed with @endforeach.

questions.text: Keep the user's dropdown choice and radio choice after a failed submission.
questions.code:
<select name="genre" class="form-select">
    <option value="Mystery" ___(old('genre') == 'Mystery')>Mystery</option>
</select>

<input type="radio" name="format" value="Hardcover"
       ___(old('format') == 'Hardcover')>
questions.explanation: @selected(condition) outputs selected on an <option>, and @checked(condition) outputs checked on a radio or checkbox, when the condition is true.

questions.text: Load the app's CSS and JS (Bootstrap is imported in them) in the page's <head>.
questions.explanation: @vite([...]) includes the Vite-built files, with parentheses rather than square brackets around the list.

questions.text: Show the logo stored at public/images/logo.png.
questions.explanation: asset('images/logo.png') builds the full URL to a file in public/.

questions.text: Add a Blade comment above the author field. It shouldn't show up in the page's HTML source.
questions.explanation: {{-- ... --}} is a Blade comment and is removed when the template compiles. An HTML <!-- --> comment would still be sent to the browser.

questions.text: After saving, send the user back to the form with a one-time success message.
questions.explanation: redirect()->back() returns to the previous page, and ->with('success', ...) flashes the message to the session for the next request only.

questions.text: Display the flashed success message on the form page.
questions.explanation: session('success') reads the value flashed by ->with('success', ...), and it is null when nothing was flashed.

questions.text: Pass the $title and $author variables to the result view in one call, using the PHP function that builds an array out of variable names.
questions.explanation: compact('title', 'author') builds ['title' => $title, 'author' => $author], and each key becomes a variable in the view.

questions.text: Print the $title variable in the result view, safely escaped.
questions.explanation: {{ $title }} echoes the value through htmlspecialchars, so any HTML a user typed is shown as text instead of being run. ({!! !!} skips the escaping.)

questions.text: Generate a migration file on its own, then generate a model together with its migration.
questions.code:
php artisan make:___ create_members_table

php artisan make:model Book ___
questions.explanation: make:migration only creates the migration. make:model Book -m creates app/Models/Book.php along with a create_books_table migration.

questions.text: Run the pending migrations, then undo the last batch.
questions.explanation: php artisan migrate runs every migration that hasn't run yet, and migrate:rollback runs the down() of the last batch.

questions.text: Complete the migration's structure.
questions.code:
<?php

use Illuminate\Database\Migrations\Migration;
use Illuminate\Database\Schema\Blueprint;
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Schema;

return new class extends Migration
{
    public function ___(): void
    {
        Schema::___('books', function (___ $table) {
            $table->id();
            $table->timestamps();
        });
    }

    public function ___(): void
    {
        Schema::___('books');
    }
};
questions.explanation: up() applies the change and down() reverses it. Schema::create makes a new table and passes a Blueprint $table to define its columns. Schema::dropIfExists('books') drops the table without erroring if it's already gone.

questions.text: Define the books columns: a unique ISBN, an optional subtitle, and created/updated timestamps.
questions.explanation: string() is a VARCHAR column. ->unique() adds a unique index and ->nullable() allows NULL. timestamps() adds created_at and updated_at.

questions.text: Pick the right column types: a long summary, a publication date, and a whole-number copy count.
questions.explanation: text() holds long text (a string column is limited to 255 characters by default). date() stores a date without a time, and integer() stores whole numbers.

questions.text: A new loan's status should be Borrowed unless something else is given.
questions.explanation: ->default('Borrowed') makes the database fill that value in when an insert leaves the column out.

questions.text: The loans table points to books, whose primary key is named book_id. Write the foreign key the long way.
questions.explanation: foreignId() creates an unsigned big integer column. ->references('book_id')->on('books') ties it to books.book_id, which you need when the primary key isn't the default id.

questions.text: The members table uses the default id primary key. Write the member_id foreign key the short way.
questions.explanation: constrained() works out the table and column from the name: member_id → members.id. It only works when the names follow that convention.

questions.text: Add a phone column to the existing members table, right after email, and remove it again in down().
questions.explanation: Schema::table changes an existing table (Schema::create would try to create it again). ->after('email') sets the column's position (MySQL/MariaDB), and dropColumn('phone') removes it.

questions.text: The model has to point to a table that isn't named books, and allow the listed fields to be mass assigned.
questions.code:
<?php

namespace App\___;

use Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\Model;

class Book extends ___
{
    protected $___ = 'library_books';

    protected $___ = [
        'isbn',
        'title',
        'copies',
    ];
}
questions.explanation: Models live in App\Models and extend Eloquent's Model. $table overrides the default table name (Book → books), and $fillable lists which fields create() may set.

questions.text: The migration used $table->id('book_id'). Tell the model, so Book::find() searches the right column.
questions.explanation: Eloquent assumes the primary key is id. If the column is book_id and $primaryKey isn't set, find(), update() and route model binding all look in a column that doesn't exist.

questions.text: Insert a row from the validated input.
questions.explanation: Book::create([...]) inserts a row and returns the model. Each key has to be in $fillable, or Laravel throws a MassAssignmentException.

questions.text: Get every book, then get one book by id, showing a 404 page if it doesn't exist.
questions.explanation: all() returns every row as a collection. findOrFail($id) returns the model or throws ModelNotFoundException, which Laravel shows as a 404. (find() would just return null.)

questions.text: Get only the Mystery books, newest first.
questions.explanation: where('genre', 'Mystery') adds the condition, and get() runs the query and returns a collection. Without get() you'd only have a query builder.

questions.text: List the books, with a fallback line when there are none.
questions.explanation: @forelse works like @foreach, but runs its @empty section when the collection has no items. It ends with @endforelse.

questions.text: The whole store method: validate, save, then redirect to the named route books.index with a flash message.
questions.explanation: validate() returns just the validated fields, so Book::create($validated) can save them directly (they're all in $fillable). redirect()->route('books.index') goes to a named route, and ->with() flashes the message.
